dedupe_keys.name: nics next generation incident command system mit lincoln laboratory open source

description: NICS is a web-based incident command and information-sharing platform that lets fire, police, medical and emergency management agencies see and edit a common incident map during disasters. MIT Lincoln Laboratory developed it with CAL FIRE, with research funding from the US Department of Homeland Security from 2010, and later released it as open source on GitHub. At its core is an incident map that overlays data from responders in the field, airborne imaging sensors, weather and traffic feeds, census data and satellite maps, with chat, whiteboard and incident archiving; a user group of more than 450 organisations shaped it, and a spin-off company received a licence in 2015 and the US Coast Guard funded a mobile app. NICS has been used for California wildfires and internationally, for example in Bosnia and Herzegovina for floods, missing persons and wildfires. The code is free to download, but the licence terms of the public repositories were not checked for this record, and the maintained commercial successor is a separate product. Caveats: the open-source release is not actively developed by the laboratory, deployment needs server administration, and the platform coordinates response, not simulating it. Simulation uses: a real-world reference for emergency response coordination exercises and digital-twin style incident dashboards, and a source of incident map layers. Related records: InaSAFE (platform-inasafe) supports impact scenarios for response planning, and the Common Alerting Protocol (data-oasis-common-alerting-protocol-cap) is a standard for exchanging alerts.
